subject.title: fix(ssh-verify): preserve active cooldown entries during prune

question: When all 512 SSH-verification cooldown slots are active, should the system preserve the existing entries and decline the new cooldown, or adopt a different explicitly bounded admission/eviction policy?
rationale: The branch’s chosen policy protects every existing active entry only by making the named hard bound ineffective; choosing the intended trade-off is a gateway reliability contract, not a mechanical correction.

options.title: Keep the cap and reject new cooldown admission
options.body: Preserve existing active cooldowns, keep the map at 512 entries, and document/test that a new cooldown is not recorded while saturated.

options.title: Use explicit bounded eviction
options.body: Keep the 512-entry cap but intentionally evict according to a documented policy, accepting that one active target may be reprobed.

options.title: Permit overflow temporarily
options.body: Allow active entries to exceed 512 only with an explicit bounded overflow limit, expiry accounting, and availability review.

recommendation.title: Keep the cap and reject new cooldown admission
recommendation.body: Preserve existing active cooldowns, keep the map at 512 entries, and document/test that a new cooldown is not recorded while saturated.
